name: Antibiotics — Broad Spectrum
summary: India's highest-volume export class. Cephalosporins and macrolides move best.
description: Broad-spectrum antibiotics are the single largest category India ships abroad by volume, spanning penicillins, cephalosporins, macrolides, fluoroquinolones and carbapenems. Freely exportable under a wholesale drug licence and RCMC for standard approved formulations. A growing number of destinations now require an antibiotic-specific import permit under antimicrobial stewardship rules, so buyers should confirm current requirements before ordering colistin or carbapenem lines in particular.

name: Anti-Tuberculosis
summary: A strategic tender category — WHO Prequalification here unlocks Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership procurement.
description: First-line and multidrug-resistant TB therapy, from the standard HRZE fixed-dose combination to newer agents like bedaquiline and delamanid, plus leprosy MDT blister packs. This is a tender-driven, high-volume, predictable-reorder category rather than a spot-market one — WHO Prequalification is effectively the entry ticket to donor-funded procurement at scale.

name: Antimalarials
summary: Artemisinin combination therapies are the mainstay; Global Fund, PMI and UNICEF are the dominant buyers.
description: Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) dominate this category, alongside older standards like chloroquine and newer options such as tafenoquine. WHO Prequalification is effectively mandatory to reach the donor-funded procurement channels — Global Fund, the President's Malaria Initiative and UNICEF — that buy the bulk of volume in this class.

name: Antiretrovirals (HIV)
summary: India supplies the majority of ARVs used in low- and middle-income countries.
description: From first-line TLD (TDF + 3TC + DTG) to newer integrase inhibitors and PrEP formulations, this class is almost entirely donor-funded and tender-driven. WHO Prequalification plus a competitive per-patient-year price is what determines access to the large procurement programmes that dominate this market.

name: Antivirals — Hepatitis, Herpes, Influenza
summary: Hepatitis C direct-acting antivirals are a landmark Indian export success story.
description: Direct-acting antivirals for hepatitis C — sofosbuvir and its combinations in particular — reach over 100 countries under voluntary licensing arrangements at a fraction of originator pricing. Licence territory should always be confirmed before quoting. The class also covers herpes, influenza and general antiviral therapy.

name: Antifungals
prescriptionNote: 3 of 39 molecules are available without prescription; the rest are prescription-only.
summary: Amphotericin B liposomal and voriconazole are hospital-tender products; topical azoles are high-volume retail lines.
description: Systemic antifungals for hospital and tender supply sit alongside high-volume topical azoles sold through pharmacy channels. Liposomal amphotericin B and voriconazole are typically hospital-tender products, while clotrimazole and terbinafine are retail staples in most destination markets.

name: Anthelmintics & Antiprotozoals
summary: Mass drug administration programmes buy these in enormous, donation-linked volumes.
description: Albendazole, ivermectin and praziquantel anchor global mass drug administration programmes against onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis and soil-transmitted helminths — a tender-driven category with very large, predictable order sizes tied to public health calendars.

name: Cardiovascular
prescriptionNote: 3 of 158 molecules are available without prescription; the rest are prescription-only.
summary: The deepest and most commoditised class. Margins are thin on older molecules; the growth is in newer anticoagulants and fixed-dose combinations.
description: From ACE inhibitors and statins to the newer direct oral anticoagulants, cardiovascular medicine is India's broadest and most commoditised export class by molecule count. Fixed-dose combinations tailored to a destination's prescribing habits are where exporters find differentiation against pure price competition.

name: Diabetes & Metabolic
prescriptionNote: 2 of 70 molecules are available without prescription.
summary: Insulins and GLP-1s sit under Schedule C/C(1), requiring Form 21B and a validated cold chain.
description: Metformin and the gliptin class are the volume workhorses of this category; insulins, GLP-1 agonists and newer agents like tirzepatide carry cold-chain and Schedule C/C(1) requirements that call for a wholesale drug licence covering biologicals (Form 21B), not just Form 20B.

name: Oncology & Immunology
exportNote: Several molecules require a CDSCO Export NOC; lenalidomide and thalidomide carry destination-specific pregnancy-prevention programme obligations.
summary: High-value and increasingly India's growth engine, from oral targeted therapies to biosimilar monoclonal antibodies.
description: Oncology is one of the fastest-growing categories in Indian pharma export, spanning cytotoxics, targeted oral therapies (TKIs), hormonal agents and a fast-expanding roster of biosimilar monoclonal antibodies. Cytotoxic manufacture requires dedicated facilities separate from general solid-dose lines, and several molecules require an Export NOC before shipment.

name: Central Nervous System & Psychiatry
exportNote: Antidepressants, antipsychotics and antiepileptics are freely exportable; every benzodiazepine and Z-drug in this class is a psychotropic under the NDPS Act requiring Narcotics Commissioner authorisation.
prescriptionNote: 2 of 167 molecules are available without prescription; 26 are NDPS-restricted.
summary: A split-personality category: freely exportable antidepressants and antiepileptics alongside NDPS-controlled benzodiazepines.
description: This class covers antidepressants, antipsychotics, antiepileptics and neurodegenerative-disease therapy — the majority freely exportable under a standard wholesale licence. Every benzodiazepine and Z-drug (alprazolam, diazepam, clonazepam, zolpidem and similar) sits in a separate, NDPS-controlled bucket requiring Narcotics Commissioner authorisation; buyers should never expect these bundled into a standard order.

name: Analgesics, NSAIDs & Opioids
exportNote: Paracetamol and the NSAIDs are freely tradable. Every opioid in this class is NDPS-controlled — the single highest-risk area in Indian pharma export today.
prescriptionNote: 7 of 78 molecules are OTC; 28 are NDPS-restricted opioids.
summary: Among India's largest-volume exports, but the category with the most active enforcement risk.
description: Paracetamol and the NSAID family are among India's largest-volume, freely-tradable exports. Opioids in this class — morphine, fentanyl, tramadol, codeine and others — are NDPS-controlled and require Narcotics Commissioner authorisation and PO-specific CDSCO clearance. Tapentadol and tapentadol–carisoprodol combinations are currently treated as off-limits following 2025 enforcement action; we do not quote these.

name: Gastrointestinal
prescriptionNote: 19 of 87 molecules are OTC.
summary: Proton pump inhibitors are a reliable, high-volume category.
description: PPIs, antiemetics and oral rehydration therapy anchor this class. Ranitidine has been withdrawn in the US, EU and many other markets over NDMA contamination concerns — we check the destination's current status before quoting it rather than relying on its Indian registration status alone.

name: Respiratory & Anti-Allergy
prescriptionNote: 16 of 80 molecules are OTC. Pseudoephedrine is a controlled precursor chemical.
summary: Metered-dose and dry-powder inhalers are a specialised manufacturing capability with far less competition than tablets.
description: Bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids and antihistamines make up the bulk of this class. Inhaler manufacture (MDI/DPI) is a genuine capability differentiator versus commodity tablet lines. Pseudoephedrine, though sold over the counter as a decongestant in many markets, is a controlled precursor chemical under NDPS rules and is handled separately.

name: Hormones, Steroids & Reproductive Health
exportNote: Corticosteroids and thyroid drugs move freely. Anabolic steroids and testosterone are controlled substances in the US and most of the EU even though not NDPS-scheduled in India.
summary: Corticosteroids and thyroid drugs move freely; abortifacient combinations are heavily restricted at both ends.
description: This class spans corticosteroids, thyroid therapy, contraceptives and reproductive-health hormones. Ulipristal/mifepristone and misoprostol combinations are Schedule H1/X in India and illegal to import in many destinations, so we treat them as an explicit-NOC, verified-buyer-only category rather than standard catalogue items.

name: Dermatology & Topicals
prescriptionNote: 21 of 81 molecules are OTC.
summary: An accessible entry category with a lower registration burden than orals in several Tier 3 markets.
description: Creams, ointments and topical antifungals carry a materially lighter registration burden than oral solid dosage forms in several Tier 3 markets, making dermatology a common first category for newer export relationships. Hydroquinone and high-potency steroid combinations are banned or restricted in the EU and several African markets — always confirmed against the destination register.

name: Ophthalmic & ENT
prescriptionNote: 9 of 75 molecules are OTC.
summary: Sterile eye drops need Form 21B and a validated sterile manufacturing line.
description: Sterile ophthalmic preparations require Form 21B and a manufacturing partner with a validated sterile fill line, distinct from standard oral solid-dose facilities. Glaucoma therapy and prostaglandin analogues are a good-margin niche within an otherwise commoditised class.

name: Vaccines & Biologicals
exportNote: Requires Form 21B, a validated cold chain, and — for UN procurement — WHO Prequalification. A manufacturer-partnership category, not one a merchant exporter enters alone.
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed — hospital, clinic and national immunisation programme use only.
summary: India supplies over 60% of global vaccine demand.
description: Vaccines, immunoglobulins and antivenoms move through UNICEF, Gavi, PAHO and national immunisation programmes rather than open-market channels. We work with manufacturing partners on Form 21B licensing and validated cold-chain logistics; this category is quoted only against a verified institutional or programme buyer.

name: Nutraceuticals, Vitamins & OTC
summary: Classified as food supplements rather than medicines in most destinations — an FSSAI licence, not a drug licence, governs this category.
description: Vitamins, minerals, protein and general wellness supplements are regulated as food supplements rather than medicines in most destination markets, which materially lightens the registration path compared to Chapter 30 pharmaceuticals. Structure-function claims are permitted; therapeutic or disease-treatment claims are not, and we keep marketing copy inside that line.

name: AYUSH — Ayurveda, Herbal & Homeopathy
summary: India's most differentiated export category and the easiest to build an international brand around.
description: Ayurvedic, Siddha, Unani and homeopathic preparations are regulated as food supplements or traditional herbal products abroad rather than as drugs in most markets. The EU novel-food catalogue should be checked before listing unusual botanicals, and heavy-metal testing is a routine buyer requirement on classical Ayurvedic formulations.

name: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs)
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed — supplied to manufacturers and formulators.
summary: India exports roughly a quarter of its pharma value as bulk drugs.
description: Active pharmaceutical ingredients and pharmaceutical intermediates supplied to international formulators and manufacturers. A European CEP or US DMF is the entry ticket to Tier 1 API buyers; Tier 2 and 3 buyers typically work off a Certificate of Analysis and an open-part dossier. Raw-material continuity from upstream KSM suppliers is a standard buyer diligence question we can help address via our manufacturing partners.

name: Medical Devices, Surgicals & Diagnostics
prescriptionNote: 25 of 96 items are OTC/consumer-purchasable; the remainder are institutional or professional-use.
summary: Regulated as devices rather than drugs — a different, often lighter, approval path.
description: Disposables, diagnostics, surgical consumables and durable medical equipment are regulated as devices rather than drugs in most destinations, which is often a materially lighter and faster approval path than the drug route. CE marking or a US 510(k) opens Tier 1 markets far more cheaply than an ANDA would for a pharmaceutical.

name: Veterinary
prescriptionNote: 3 of 68 items are available without prescription.
summary: An under-served corridor with less competition than human generics and a lighter registration burden in most Tier 3 markets.
description: Veterinary antiparasitics, antibiotics, vaccines and feed-additive products for livestock and companion animals. Registration burden is materially lighter than the human-generic equivalent in most Tier 3 markets, making this a defensible niche for exporters willing to build the relationships.

name: Anaesthesia, Sedation & Neuromuscular Blockade
exportNote: Propofol, volatile agents and muscle relaxants are freely exportable; ketamine, midazolam and every opioid here are NDPS-controlled and require Narcotics Commissioner authorisation.
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed — hospital and surgical-tender use only.
summary: A hospital-tender category with far fewer competitors than oral generics, but a mixed control status.
description: General anaesthetic agents, local anaesthetics and neuromuscular blocking agents for hospital and surgical-tender supply. This class has a mixed control status within itself: propofol, volatile agents and muscle relaxants are freely exportable, while ketamine, midazolam and opioid agents require full NDPS narcotics authorisation and are quoted on separate invoices.

name: Emergency, Critical Care & Resuscitation
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed — hospital and government procurement.
summary: Essential-medicine list products that every ministry of health buys on repeat tender.
description: Emergency and resuscitation medicines drawn from the WHO Essential Medicines List — low margin per unit but high volume with predictable, repeat reorder cycles. A steady category for establishing a long-term institutional supply relationship.

name: Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Fertility
exportNote: Uterotonics and maternal-health commodities are core institutional-tender lines. Abortifacient combinations are Schedule H1/X in India and prohibited in many destinations, so we handle those only with explicit NOC and a verified import permit.
prescriptionNote: 8 of 54 molecules are OTC; 2 are restricted.
summary: Heat-stable carbetocin and oxytocin are a genuine Indian strength in maternal-health commodities.
description: Uterotonics, antenatal supplements and fertility therapy for institutional and ministry-tender buyers. Heat-stable carbetocin and oxytocin, core UNFPA and ministry-of-health tender lines, are a genuine area of Indian manufacturing strength.

name: Urology & Nephrology
prescriptionNote: 3 of 54 molecules are OTC.
summary: Phosphate binders, ESAs and ketoanalogues sell into dialysis chains expanding fast across Africa and SE Asia.
description: BPH and overactive-bladder therapy provide steady retail-channel volume, while the nephrology side — phosphate binders, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, iron and ketoanalogues — sells into dialysis chains that are expanding rapidly across Africa and South-East Asia.

name: Rheumatology, Gout & Immunosuppressants
prescriptionNote: 1 of 49 molecules is OTC.
summary: Biosimilars of anti-TNF agents are one of India's strongest high-value export stories.
description: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs and a fast-growing roster of biosimilar biologics (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab and others) sell at a large discount to originator pricing in Tier 2 and 3 markets. Transplant immunosuppressants need narrow-therapeutic-index bioequivalence data, so manufacturer selection matters more here than in ordinary generics.

name: Haematology & Blood Disorders
prescriptionNote: 8 of 48 molecules are OTC.
summary: Thalassaemia and sickle-cell belts across Africa, the Mediterranean and South Asia make iron chelators a durable niche.
description: Iron chelators, hydroxyurea and recombinant clotting factors serve the thalassaemia and sickle-cell belts spanning Africa, the Mediterranean and South Asia. Recombinant clotting factors and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents require Form 21B and a validated cold chain.

name: Antidotes & Clinical Toxicology
summary: A small but strategically useful category — ministries and disaster-preparedness programmes stockpile these on tender.
description: Antidotes and toxicology stock for ministry and disaster-preparedness programmes, where competition is thin because individual volumes are unattractive to large suppliers. Anti-snake venom in particular is chronically short across Africa and South Asia and is a good relationship-building line.

name: IV Fluids, Electrolytes & Parenteral Nutrition
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed.
summary: Heavy, low-value-per-kilo goods, so freight economics decide whether this works.
description: IV fluids and parenteral nutrition are heavy, low-value-per-kilo goods where freight economics — not registration — usually decides whether an export lane makes sense. Best suited to nearby or coastal markets, or bundled alongside higher-value product lines in the same shipment.

name: Contrast Media, Radiopharmaceuticals & In-Vivo Diagnostics
exportNote: Radiopharmaceuticals carry AERB licensing and short half-lives that make export logistics genuinely difficult — a later-stage speciality, not a starting line.
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed.
summary: Iodinated and gadolinium contrast agents are a solid, high-repeat imaging-chain product.
description: Contrast agents for CT and MRI imaging are a steady, high-repeat product line for imaging-chain buyers. Radiopharmaceuticals sit in the same HS heading but carry separate AERB licensing and short half-lives that make logistics genuinely hard — we treat that sub-segment as a later-stage specialism.

name: Blood Products & Plasma Derivatives
exportNote: Raw human blood cannot be exported. Fractionated plasma derivatives can, but require central licensing, a licensed fractionation partner, and destination-specific plasma-sourcing documentation.
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed.
summary: High-value and supply-constrained worldwide.
description: Fractionated plasma derivatives — human albumin, immunoglobulins and clotting-factor concentrates — supplied through licensed fractionation partners under central licensing. High-value, chronically supply-constrained globally, and quoted only against verified hospital or government buyers.

name: Rare Disease, Orphan & Specialty Biologics
exportNote: Much of this trade moves as named-patient or compassionate-use supply — expect purchase-order-specific quantities and heavy documentation.
prescriptionNote: Not retail-dispensed.
summary: India is becoming a serious source of affordable enzyme replacement and orphan therapies.
description: Enzyme replacement therapy and orphan-disease biologics, offered largely as named-patient or compassionate-use supply — precisely the case an Export NOC exists for. Expect purchase-order-specific quantities and a heavier documentation load than standard generics.

name: Antiseptics, Disinfectants & Hospital Hygiene
summary: Often classified as biocides rather than medicines, usually meaning a lighter registration path.
description: Antiseptics and hospital-hygiene products are frequently classified outside Chapter 30 as biocides rather than medicines, which typically means a lighter registration path — though the EU's own biocidal-products regime can be stricter than its drug route, so destination rules are checked either way.

name: Dental & Oral Care
summary: Dental materials are regulated as devices in most markets — a materially faster, cheaper registration route than drugs.
description: Dental restorative materials, endodontic products and oral-care consumables sit under HS 3006.40 and are regulated as devices, not drugs, in most markets. India's dental materials industry is strong and price-competitive, and this remains an under-exploited export corridor relative to pharmaceuticals.
